title: Opaque fragment protocol for SSE + client graceful-rejoin behavior
creator: Amelia Zhang
description:
Problem: Clients observe truncated or duplicated function-call/tool-call structured outputs when reconnecting to SSE. Current resume approaches depend on servers understanding and reassembling semantic fragments (function-call boundaries / JSONL messages). That couples runtime and API semantics and increases complexity for proxying and CDN-like edge layers.

Goal: Design and implement an opaque-fragment SSE protocol that: (1) treats server-produced fragments as opaque delivery units for the transport layer, (2) provides deterministic, idempotent fragment identifiers and checksums so clients can reconcile duplicate/partial deliveries, (3) preserves atomicity guarantees for function/tool calls and structured JSONL outputs without requiring the transport stack to parse content, (4) defines a minimal client-server handshake to support graceful rejoin, stash/resend, and limited server-side playback for short window reconnections.

Scope of work:
- Define event headers / metadata fields (SEGMENT-ID, SEQ, START-OFFSET, CHUNK-CHECKSUM, CHUNK-TYPE, FINAL-BYTE-LENGTH) and their serialization in the SSE event envelope. These fields must be ASCII and tolerant of proxies and EventSource polyfills.
- Choose checksum algorithm (xxhash64) and canonicalization rules (UTF-8 bytes, no normalization, explicit escaping for stream-level sentinel bytes) so checksum is deterministic across language runtimes.
- Establish opaque semantics: runtime must not make content-level assumptions about segmentation except for marking segments that are atomic (CHUNK-TYPE=atomic) vs streaming (CHUNK-TYPE=partial). Function/tool calls must be emitted as CHUNK-TYPE=atomic or wrapped inside a clearly delimited atomic manifest segment.
- Client handshake: on reconnect, client sends last-acknowledged SEGMENT-ID+byte-offset and optional recent checksum window. Server responds with a short manifest of segments available for replay (IDs, seq ranges, lengths) and a replay token. Manifest is capped (e.g., last 512 segments) to limit memory.
- Replay strategy: Server may replay complete segments only (no mid-segment patching). If the reconnect point is mid-segment, client must request either (a) replay previous full segment(s) and accept duplication, or (b) fallback to an out-of-band poll for final assembly. We will document both flows.
- Atomic function/toolcall guarantees: Producers must ensure that segments containing tool/function call start and end are emitted as a single atomic segment. If a function call exceeds segment-size targets, the runtime should pin it to an atomic storage object and emit a short proxy segment referencing that object (SEG-REF). Client will then fetch the object via secure URL if necessary (implementation detail for Private deployments).
- Backoff/hedging: define probe TTL and jittered exponential backoff for reconnect attempts. Include a lightweight probe event (type: PROBE) that exercises server-side session validity without replaying heavy payloads.
- Compatibility: provide EventSource-friendly fallbacks: avoid binary-only headers, use optional JSON-serialized metadata field in SSE data for intermediaries that strip custom headers. Also provide a chunked-HTTP fallback endpoint for proxies that cannot maintain SSE.
- Observability: emit metrics at segment emission (segment_size, segment_latency, checksum_mismatch_count) and reconciliation metrics on reconnect (replays_issued, client_conflicts).
- Tests: unit tests for checksum canonicalization, integration tests simulating proxy-induced truncation, chaos tests for rapid connect/disconnect patterns, and benchmark for p95 reconnect latency under 1k concurrent clients.

Design trade-offs and decisions taken so far:
- Use opaque segments to simplify edge proxies and avoid content sniffing at every hop. Trade-off: clients must accept some duplication upon reconnect; we will surface deduplication helpers in SDKs.
- Chosen checksum: xxhash64 for speed and low collision risk; validated against small corpus of generated JSONL and function call payloads.
- Manifest window size set to 512 segments (configurable per deployment). Larger windows increase memory but reduce client-initiated full polls.
- Atomic segment reference (SEG-REF) allows emitting large structured outputs without enlarging transport segments; requires safe temporary object storage and secure URLs for Private deployments.

Open questions / risks: 
- Should we require all tool/function-call outputs to be atomic segments by default? Enforcing that increases latency for very large responses. Proposal: default atomic for tool calls, but allow opt-in streaming for long-running tool outputs with explicit SDK support.
- How long to retain segment manifests in Dedicated and Hosted tiers before GC? Impacts memory and storage. Proposal: Hosted default 5 minutes, Dedicated configurable 1-60 minutes.
- Compatibility with existing SSE resume tokens: we will provide a compatibility shim that accepts previous resume tokens and translates into the manifest-based handshake where possible.

Deliverables:
- RFC doc with protocol fields, examples, and fallbacks (Confluence link below).
- Implementation: runtime encoder/decoder (Go), proxy shim (Node) for edge layer, SDK helpers for client-side reconcilers (Python/TS).
- Test harness + perf dashboard sample.

Links and artifacts:
- Design RFC (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SSE+Opaque+Fragment+Protocol (draft)
- Draft PR for runtime encoding: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3128 (WIP)
- SDK dedupe helper draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/459 (WIP)
- Bench harness: https://dash.redwood.ai/bench/streaming/reconnect-2026 (private)

Next steps (this ticket):
1) Finalize header names and canonicalization rules (owner: Diego).
2) Implement server-side segment manifest cache and replay endpoint (owner: Backend infra).
3) Add SSE metadata encoder in runtime emitter and a compatibility shim in edge proxy (owner: Diego + Alexei).
4) Add SDK dedupe utility and sample integration in chat demo (owner: SDK lead).
5) Run integration tests and capture reconnect p95/p99; verify function-call atomicity in chaos tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- RFC approved by PM and Security reviewer.
- Runtime emits SEGMENT-ID, SEQ, CHUNK-CHECKSUM headers for SSE events.
- Client can reconnect and reconcile without content-level parsing by the transport stack; guide and SDK dedupe helper available.
- No regression in streaming p95 latency (target: < 50ms additional overhead per segment).
comments: 2026-03-01 - Amelia Zhang: Created ticket. Initial scoping and tradeoffs captured. Assigned to Diego to prototype header naming and checksum canonicalization.

2026-03-03 - Diego Ruiz: Prototype emitter implemented locally. Using xxhash64; canonicalization: raw UTF-8 bytes, no trimming. Found a proxy that strips non-standard SSE event fields—added JSON-metadata data field as fallback for compatibility.

2026-03-04 - Priya Menon (PM): Reviewed goals. Emphasized that tool-call atomicity is critical for customers with webhook-like tool integrations. Requested explicit error modes for when SEG-REF retrieval fails.

2026-03-05 - Diego Ruiz: Created draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3128. Added segment manifest cache with LRU eviction. Local tests simulate mid-segment disconnect and client dedupe flow.

2026-03-07 - Security review (Suresh Patel): Flagged SEG-REF approach for Private deployments — must ensure signed, short-lived URLs and audit logging. Requested threat model write-up. Marked security_review_required.

2026-03-08 - Alexei Morozov (Edge): Implemented Node proxy shim that converts custom headers into data metadata to make it compatible with CloudLoadBalancer that strips headers. Integration test passing locally.

2026-03-09 - QA (Lin Huang): Created integration tests for 200 client reconnects per second. Observed ~0.8% checksum_mismatch_count in initial run; investigating canonicalization differences between Python and Go emitters.

2026-03-10 - Diego Ruiz: Fixed canonicalization bug (Python SDK used "
" normalization). Re-ran tests; mismatch dropped to 0.01%. Preparing RFC for RFC review board next week.
